prompts.prompt: How could ships at sea tell the Gannet Rock light apart from the other lights on the coast?
prompts.answer: Every light on the coast had its own pattern of flashes, and sailors counted them. Gannet Rock gave one white flash every ten seconds, which no other light on the coast did.

prompts.prompt: Why did the keepers have to keep winding the clockwork all through the night?
prompts.answer: A heavy iron weight sinking down the tower drove the gears that turned the lens. When the weight reached the bottom the lens stopped, and a still light was worse than no light, because a ship might mistake it for another. So the weight had to be wound back up every four hours, with forty turns of a crank.

prompts.prompt: Why did the keepers have to rely on the fog horn rather than the lamp on foggy nights?
prompts.answer: In fog the lamp's beam was swallowed within a few yards of the glass, so the light was almost useless and a ship could run onto the rocks without ever seeing it. The keepers had to warn ships by sound instead, with a horn giving two blasts every minute.

prompts.prompt: How did the young fisherman manage to reach the lighthouse on the ninth night of fog?
prompts.answer: His engine had failed, so he rowed across from the mainland, steering only by the sound of the fog horn (two blasts, then silence) until his boat grounded on the shingle below the tower.

prompts.prompt: What did Dr. Vane say the green light on the water was, and what did it show?
prompts.answer: Phosphorescence: light made by tiny living creatures when the water is disturbed. It was not dangerous; it showed that the water was full of plankton, which meant there would be fish.

prompts.prompt: What did Dr. Vane's study of the old logbooks show about the fog signal, and why had nobody noticed it before?
prompts.answer: Over nineteen years the horn had sounded for more than four thousand hours, and nearly half of those hours fell in November and December. Nobody had noticed because, as Ione said, a keeper only ever sees one night at a time.

prompts.prompt: What did Ione do on the nights when the clockwork stopped, and why?
prompts.answer: She climbed into the lamp room and turned the great lens by hand until dawn, so that passing ships would still see the light's one white flash every ten seconds. It had happened only three times in nineteen years.
